quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: If you lock your rear brake by accident on a road with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear wheel on a road with good traction, keep it locked until you stop. On good pavement, you can control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel as long as the bike is upright and going straight.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is easiest to see when riding in which lane position?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, ride in the center of your lane. This position puts you in the driver's rearview mirror and makes you more visible. Be ready to change position if needed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must not go over the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not go over the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: To make a quick turn, you should:

options.text: Shift your body weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Make your motorcycle lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make your motorcycle lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To make an evasive turn, you need to lean your motorcycle quickly in the direction you want to turn. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Show a narrow view of the road behind you.
Show a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Someone is following you too closely.
You will slow down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as bright as a car's. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so others notice you are slowing down. This is especially important if you are slowing faster than expected.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The trailer adds weight, so your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely need to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Keep the tire pressure the same.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure settings.

questions.question: What formation should you use when riding in a group?

options.text: Always single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal is about to change to red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left part of the lane, next to the centerline.
The right part of the lane, next to the curb.
It can change based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space around you. Change your position as traffic and road conditions change.

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that is right for the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You may not be able to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the vehicle could swerve into your lane or hit you. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When should a staggered formation NOT be used by a group of motorcyclists?

options.text: It should always be used.
When entering or leaving a highway.
When riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation most of the time. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Before you start riding, you should make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Before you ride, open the fuel supply valve on your motorcycle. If the valve is closed, the engine may start but will stop once the remaining fuel in the lines is used up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, look for other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing a truck, only return to your original lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is usually the best choice, but this can change depending on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: What is the legal blood alcohol content (BAC) limit for a driver of legal drinking age?

options.text: .02 percent
.08 percent
.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: .08 percent
questions.explanation: A driver of legal drinking age is legally intoxicated at .08 percent BAC. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You can go over the speed limit until the pass is finished.
You can ignore no passing zone markings if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must happen within the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Speed up.
Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead.
Stay closer to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase the distance between you and other vehicles to prevent crashes. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Leave more space to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger handles differently due to the extra weight. Ride slower and allow more time to stop. A passenger should hold firmly onto the motorcycle's passenger grips or onto the rider's waist, hips, or midsection—not the back of the bike.
